mainTopic: How ציצית are tied and wound: the Torah status of the top knot, torn strings, the winding string, and the number and order of the windings.
overview: The amud opens by rejecting a proof that a knot is needed between each set of windings: the sons of רבי חייא may have tied those knots by choice. רבה then proves that the top knot (קשר עליון) is דאורייתא. Without a real knot, wool ציצית on a linen garment would not count as joined, so the Torah would not have needed to permit כלאים there. רב rules that a string torn at its base makes the ציצית פסולה. רבא challenges this from a ברייתא about leftover and torn strings, and the גמרא answers that the ברייתא means the remainder of torn strings, which must still be long enough to tie a loop. Next come two rulings: the winding string counts as one of the strings, and winding most of the strings is still כשר. In each case רב יוסף corrects which sage said it. A fuller version adds that even one חוליא is כשר, and the nicest look is one-third winding and two-thirds loose. A חוליא is at least three windings, and the ideal is seven to thirteen sets, matching the רקיעים and the air spaces between them. The windings start and end with white. The amud ends by starting a story about a man in a cloak made entirely of תכלת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe they tied knots by choice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier proof: the sons of רבי חייא may have tied knots between the windings even though there is no obligation to do so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps they tied knots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof it just brought. What the sons of רבי חייא did does not prove that a knot is required between each set of windings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof assumed that whatever they did was required. The rejection says they may simply have chosen to tie extra knots. Their behavior therefore shows what is allowed, not what is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / maybe. Often opens a rejection of a proof.
He tied a knot (from קֶטֶר, a knot).

phrases.english: Perhaps it is a case where he tied knots.
phrases.notes: This pushes back on the proof just before, from the sons of רבי חייא: maybe they tied the knots by choice, not because they had to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought just before this text from the practice of the sons of רבי חייא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a knot between each set of windings is required.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An action that someone chose to do does not prove an obligation. They may have tied knots without being required to.

steps.title: The top knot is required by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבה proves that the קשר עליון is דאורייתא. Otherwise the Torah would have no need to permit wool ציצית on a linen garment, since one loose connection does not count as joining the two materials anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Learn from this that the top knot is required by Torah law. If you thought it was only rabbinic, why would the Torah need to permit wool ציצית on a linen garment? That would be obvious, because joining two things with one single stitch is not considered a connection. So learn from this that the knot is required by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a logical proof that tying the top knot of the ציצית is a Torah requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah specially permits כלאים (wool and linen together) for ציצית. If the Torah only required pulling the strings through the hole with no knot, the wool and linen would not count as joined, just like one single stitch, and no special permission would be needed. Since the Torah did need to permit it, the strings must be joined by a real knot, so the knot is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The top knot, the knot closest to the garment.
Required by Torah law.
Required only by rabbinic law.
It is obvious, so why say it?
A single stitch or connection.
A connection that legally joins two things.

steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the top knot a Torah requirement of ציצית, not just a rabbinic addition.

phrases.english: And רבה said: Learn from this
that the top knot is required by Torah law.
For if it enters your mind that it is rabbinic,
why was it necessary to permit a linen cloak with ציצית?
phrases.notes: He means wool ציצית on a linen garment, which would normally be forbidden as כלאים.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
One who attaches with a single stitch has not made a connection.
phrases.notes: For כלאים, joining wool and linen with just one stitch does not count as joining them.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this that it is required by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the windings to a new point about the status of the top knot.
steps.raayaObject: That the קשר עליון of ציצית is required by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's permission of כלאים in ציצית, together with the rule that a single stitch is not a connection.

steps.title: A string torn at its base makes the ציצית unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a ציצית string tears at its base, where it meets the garment, the ציצית are פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב אדא said in the name of רב אדא, who said in the name of רב: If the string was severed at its base, the ציצית are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is introduced about a ציצית string that tears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is about a tear at the root of the string, right by the garment. רב says this makes the ציצית unfit, apparently even after they were made properly. This sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Was severed or torn.
At its base, where it is attached to the garment.
Unfit, invalid for the מצוה.

steps.confusionAlert: Here מעיקרו means at the base of the string, a place. It does not mean 'from the beginning' in time.

phrases.english: רבה בר רב אדא said
that רב אדא said that רב said:
If the string was severed at its base, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: torn ציצית strings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a ציצית string tears at its base, the ציצית are פסולה.

steps.title: רבא challenges from a ברייתא allowing leftover strings
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן taught רב's ruling, and רבא challenged him from a ברייתא. The minimum length applies only when the ציצית are first made; afterwards, leftover and torn strings are fine at any length.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן sat and taught this ruling. רבא challenged רב נחמן: When does this apply? At the beginning. But at the end, its leftovers and its torn pieces are fit at any length.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב's ruling that a torn string makes the ציצית unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates the start, when the strings must be long enough, from later, after the ציצית were made properly. At that later stage, even small leftover or torn pieces are fine. This seems to say a torn string does not make the ציצית unfit, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling.
At its beginning, when first made.
Its end, after it was made properly.
Its leftovers, what remains of the strings.
Its cut-off or torn pieces.
Any amount at all, even tiny.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן וְקָא אָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: רב נחמן sat and was teaching this ruling.
רבא raised an objection to רב נחמן:
When is this said? At its beginning.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that the strings need a minimum length.

phrases.english: But at its end,
its leftovers and its torn pieces are fit at any length.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a string torn at its base makes the ציצית פסולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that after the ציצית were made properly, torn pieces of any length are fit. That suggests a tear does not make the ציצית unfit.

steps.title: Explaining 'leftovers' and 'torn pieces' to sharpen the challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא's terms: שיריו means some strings tore and some remain, and גרדומיו means strings that were completely torn off. Both are fit, which seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are 'its leftovers' and what are 'its torn pieces'? Is it not that 'its leftovers' means some strings tore and some remain, and 'its torn pieces' means they were completely cut down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines the two words in the ברייתא to show exactly why it seems to contradict רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מאי לאו' offers a reading that makes the challenge stronger. If גרדומיו means strings torn all the way down, the ברייתא allows even a fully torn string. That is very close to רב's case of a string torn at its base, which he called unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that…? Offers a reading that supports the challenge.
Was cut or torn.
Remained, was left over.
Was cut down or chopped off.

phrases.english: What are 'its leftovers' and what are 'its torn pieces'?
Is it not that 'its leftovers' means
that some of them were torn and some of them remained,
and 'its torn pieces' means that they were completely cut down?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁיָרָיו וּמַאי גַּרְדּוּמָּיו? מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sharpens רבא's challenge by defining the terms of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a string torn at its base makes the ציצית פסולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If גרדומיו means strings cut down completely and they are still fit, then a torn string does not make the ציצית unfit, against רב.

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches one rule, not two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבא: the ברייתא does not list two separate cases. It teaches one rule, that the remainder of severed strings is fit at any length.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The ברייתא teaches one rule: the remainder of its severed strings is fit at any length.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It rereads the ברייתא as one rule instead of two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read שיריו and גרדומיו as two cases, and one of them seemed to clash with רב. The new reading joins them into one phrase: 'the remainder of its severed strings.' So the strings are only partly cut, and some length is still left. That is different from a string torn right at its base, which is רב's case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is teaching one thing (one rule, not two)
The remainder, what is left over
Any amount at all

phrases.english: No, it is teaching one ruling:
the remainder of its severed strings is fit at any length.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 4-5 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: two terms become one combined phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists two cases, and one of them is strings torn off completely, which would clash with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only of what remains of the severed strings, so it says nothing against רב.

steps.title: Then why mention 'remainder' at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the point is about severed strings, the ברייתא could have just said 'its severed strings.' Why add the word 'remainder'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let it just say 'its severed strings.' Why do I need the word 'its remainder'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the new reading. It asks why the extra word is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in a ברייתא teaches something. If the case is only about severed strings, the word שיריו seems extra. The next step must explain what that word adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (Why is this word needed?)
And let it say (then it should have said)

phrases.english: Then let it say: "its severed strings";
why do I need "its remainder"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording behind the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא given in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is about severed strings, the word 'remainder' seems extra.

steps.title: Enough must be left to tie a loop
steps.stepSummary: The word 'remainder' teaches a minimum: the severed strings must still have enough length left to tie them in a loop.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that the severed strings need a leftover long enough to tie them in a loop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the extra word adds. Even severed strings must keep enough length to be tied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any length' does not mean literally nothing is left. The word שיריו sets a minimum: enough to tie a loop around the other strings. Now every word in the ברייתא has a job, and רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
To tie them in a loop (a slipknot)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is about what is left of torn strings, so it does not contradict רב. Even torn strings must be long enough to tie a loop.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that we require a remainder of its severed strings
long enough to tie them in a loop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the extra word teaches a new detail
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches the minimum length: enough left to tie a loop.

steps.title: The winding string counts as one of the strings
steps.stepSummary: רבה says in רב's name that the string used for winding counts toward the required number of ציצית strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה sat and said in רב's name: the string used for winding counts toward the number of strings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה gives a ruling about the string that is wrapped around the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One string is wrapped around the rest to make the windings. The question is whether it must be an extra string. The ruling is no: it is one of the regular strings, so no additional string is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The winding string, the one wrapped around the others
Counts toward the required number

phrases.english: Rabba sat and said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: חוּט שֶׁל כֶּרֶךְ עוֹלֶה מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: The winding string counts toward the number.
phrases.notes: The 'number' is the set of strings on each corner, so the winding string is one of them, not an extra.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about winding the ציצית strings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The winding string is one of the counted strings.

steps.title: רב יוסף: It was שמואל, not רב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף corrects רבה: the ruling about the winding string was said by שמואל, not by רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: שמואל said it, not רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף fixes who said the ruling. He does not argue with the ruling itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה stays the same. Only the name attached to it changes from רב to שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Said it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
Shmuel said it, and not Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects who said the ruling in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the attribution, not the ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling was given in the wrong sage's name.

steps.title: Another chain reports the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: The same ruling is also reported by רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יאשיה of אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבה בר בר חנה said, רבי יאשיה of אושא told me that the winding string counts toward the number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another report of the same ruling. This shows it was known in another chain too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second, separate chain teaches the same rule. This backs up the ruling itself: the winding string counts as one of the strings.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a supporting report)
Told me

steps.whatToRemember: The winding string is one of the regular ציצית strings. No extra string is needed.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:

phrases.aramaic: סָח לִי רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה דְּמִן אוּשָׁא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya of Usha told me:

phrases.aramaic: חוּט שֶׁל כֶּרֶךְ עוֹלָה לָהּ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: The winding string counts toward the number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support for the ruling of step 9 from another chain.
steps.raayaObject: That the winding string counts toward the number
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה quoting רבי יאשיה of אושא

steps.title: Winding most of the strings is still כשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says in שמואל's name: if the windings cover most of the strings' length, the ציצית are still כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא sat and said in שמואל's name: תכלת strings that were wound for most of their length are כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling about how much of the strings may be wound. Even if most of the length is wound, the ציצית are fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally most of the strings hang loose below the windings. This ruling says that if someone wound more than half, the ציצית are still fit, even though it is not the usual way.

keyTerms.meaning: The sky-blue string(s) of ציצית
That he wound most of it
Fit, valid

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָא אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rava sat and said in the name of Shmuel:
Sky-blue strings that he wound for most of their length are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבָא וְקָא אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about winding, set up the same way as step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Winding most of the strings does not make the ציצית פסול.

steps.title: רב יוסף: It was רב, not שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף again corrects who said it: this ruling was said by רב, not by שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: רב said it, not שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like before, רב יוסף fixes the name on the ruling. The ruling itself stays the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 10. There, a ruling given in רב's name was really שמואל's. Here, a ruling given in שמואל's name is really רב's.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two corrections. The winding-string ruling belongs to שמואל, and the 'wound most of it' ruling belongs to רב.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
Rav said it, and not Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects who said the ruling in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the attribution, not the ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling was given in the wrong sage's name.

steps.title: A chain of רבנן confirms it was רב
steps.stepSummary: A report passed from רב through רב ירמיה בר אבא, רב ששת and רב הונא בר יהודה confirms that רב said this ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת, in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא, in the name of רב: תכלת strings that were wound for most of their length are כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב יוסף. It shows a chain of teachers that traces this ruling back to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain ends with רב himself, so it supports רב יוסף's correction. The ruling stays the same: winding most of the strings is still כשר.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Huna bar Yehuda said
that Rav Sheshet said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
Sky-blue strings that he wound for most of their length are fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's correction in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling 'wound most of it is כשר' is רב's
steps.raayaSupportSource: The chain of רב הונא בר יהודה, רב ששת and רב ירמיה בר אבא, reaching back to רב

steps.title: Even one set of windings works, and the nicest look is one-third winding
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב נתן teaches a longer version of רב's ruling. Winding most of the strings is כשר. Even a single set of windings is כשר. The nicest look is one-third winding and two-thirds loose strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא son of רב נתן taught it this way: רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת, in the name of רב ירמיה בר אבא, in the name of רב: תכלת strings wound for most of their length are כשר. Even if he wound only one set of windings, they are כשר. The nicest way is one-third windings and two-thirds loose strings.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teacher gives a fuller version of the same chain. He adds two new points: the smallest amount of winding allowed, and the nicest way to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version sets both edges. Winding a lot (most of the strings) is fit, and winding very little (just one חוליא) is also fit. The ideal, for beauty, is one-third winding and two-thirds hanging loose.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it this way (gives a different version)
One set of windings, one 'link'
The beauty of, the nicest way to do
The wound, braided part
The loose part hanging like branches

steps.whatToRemember: Winding most of the strings or only one חוליא is still כשר. The nicest way is one-third winding and two-thirds loose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical picture of ציצית: most of the length hangs loose, and the winding takes up about one-third.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן מַתְנֵי הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rav Natan, teaches it like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא, אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav Sheshet said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
Sky-blue strings that he wound for most of their length are fit,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ לֹא כָּרַךְ בָּהּ אֶלָּא חוּלְיָא אַחַת – כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: and even if he wound only one set of windings, they are fit,
and the nicest way to do the sky-blue strings is
one-third windings and two-thirds loose strings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן מַתְנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fuller version of the ruling in step 14, with two added points.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Winding most of the strings or only one חוליא is כשר. The ideal is one-third winding and two-thirds loose.

steps.title: How big is one set of windings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the minimum size of one חוליא is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the measure of one set of windings?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier steps said that even one חוליא is כשר. Now the גמרא asks how much winding counts as one חוליא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said a single חוליא is enough, but it never said how big a חוליא has to be. Without a minimum, the rule has no clear meaning, so the גמרא asks for the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A required measure or minimum amount
A set or group of windings around the ציצית strings

phrases.english: And how much is the measure of a set of windings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size of the חוליא mentioned in רב's ruling in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum number of windings that make up one חוליא.

steps.title: A set is at least three windings
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that one חוליא means winding once, a second time and a third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: enough that he winds once, winds a second time and winds a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. רבי says one חוליא is three windings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three verbs, wind, repeat, and do a third time, set the minimum at three turns of the string. Fewer than three turns does not count as a חוליא.

keyTerms.meaning: That he winds (wraps the string around)
And does it a second time
And does it a third time

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says:
Enough that he winds, and winds a second time, and winds a third time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חוליא is at least three windings.

steps.title: Between seven and thirteen sets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one should make no fewer than seven sets and no more than thirteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: one who makes fewer should not make fewer than seven, and one who adds should not add beyond thirteen.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the proper range for how many sets of windings to make: from seven up to thirteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said one חוליא is already כשר, so this range is about the proper way to do the מצוה, not the bare minimum. Someone making few sets should still make seven, and someone making many should stop at thirteen.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes fewer (the person choosing the smaller number)
One who adds (the person choosing the larger number)
Thirteen

steps.confusionAlert: The seven and thirteen here count sets (חוליות), not single windings. Each set itself has at least three windings, as רבי said in step 17.

phrases.english: It was taught: One who minimizes should not have fewer than seven,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמּוֹסִיף לֹא יוֹסִיף עַל שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: and one who adds should not add beyond thirteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining one חוליא, gives the proper number of חוליות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ideal number of sets is between seven and thirteen.

steps.title: Why seven and why thirteen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that seven matches the seven רקיעים, and thirteen matches the seven רקיעים plus the six spaces of air between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who minimizes should not have fewer than seven, matching the seven heavens. One who adds should not go beyond thirteen, matching the seven heavens and the six air spaces between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's two numbers and gives a reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven matches the seven רקיעים. Thirteen adds the six spaces between those seven רקיעים, so 7 + 6 = 13. The numbers are not random; they picture the heavens.

keyTerms.meaning: Matching, corresponding to
Heavens, layers of sky
Spaces of air

phrases.english: One who minimizes should not have fewer than seven,
corresponding to the seven firmaments,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַמּוֹסִיף לֹא יוֹסִיף עַל שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: and one who adds should not add beyond thirteen,
corresponding to the seven firmaments
and the six air spaces that are between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפּוֹחֵת לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשֶּׁבַע, כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעָה רְקִיעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ברייתא from step 18 to give the reason behind its numbers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven sets match the seven רקיעים; thirteen match the seven רקיעים plus the six air spaces between them.

steps.title: Start and finish the windings with white
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the windings begin with white because of the word הכנף, and end with white because we go up in holiness and not down.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when he begins, he begins with white, because of 'the corner', the same kind as the corner. When he finishes, he finishes with white, because we go up in holiness and do not go down.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא tells us which color string to use at the start and at the end of the windings. Both times the answer is white.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting with white comes from the פסוק's word הכנף: the white strings match the garment's corner, so they come first. Ending with white rests on a different reason: once you started with white, finishing with something else would be going down in holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: White (the white strings of the ציצית)
The same kind as the corner of the garment
In holy matters we go up and do not go down

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין appears in many places in ש״ס. Here it shapes even the order of colors in ציצית.

phrases.english: It was taught: When he begins –
he begins with the white:
"The corner" – the same type as the corner,
and when he finishes – he finishes with the white,
for we elevate in holiness and do not downgrade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the number of sets, gives the order of colors in the windings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The windings begin with white, learned from הכנף, and end with white, because מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין.
steps.whatToRemember: A חוליא is at least three windings. The ideal is seven to thirteen sets, matching the רקיעים and the air between them. The windings start and end with white.

steps.title: A man walks by in a cloak made all of תכלת
steps.stepSummary: A story begins: רב and רבה בר בר חנה were sitting, and a man passed by wearing a cloak made entirely of תכלת, with תכלת strings attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבה בר בר חנה were sitting. A certain man was passing by, wearing a cloak made entirely of תכלת, and he had attached תכלת strings to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story to set up the next discussion. Here we only see the scene, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that the whole cloak is תכלת is the key point. It makes us wonder how ציצית strings work when the garment itself is already the color of the תכלת string. The reaction of the two sages comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Were sitting
Passing by and going along
A cloak
תכלת, sky-blue wool

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲווֹ יָתְבִי,
phrases.english: Rav and Rabba bar bar Ḥana were sitting,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא חָלֵיף וְאָזֵיל הָהוּא גַּבְרָא
phrases.english: a certain man was passing by
who was wearing a cloak that was entirely sky-blue wool,
and he had put sky-blue strings on it

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story connected to ציצית with תכלת, moving away from the rules about windings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a cloak made entirely of תכלת with ציצית on it; the ruling comes later.
